newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end up after bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end up after bargain-hunting.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed higher on Monday following bargain-hunting in selected big-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index rose 4.67 points, or 0.73 percent, to close at 642.26 points after touching a day high of 643.38 points. Advancers led decliners by 74 to 48 with 72 issues unchanged.
"We expect the slight rebound to continue, but the index is unlikely to cross the 650 levels until after the election in May," one analyst who declined to be named said.

"Investors should look out for rebounds in blue-chip stocks after the elections in May and some volatile property sector trading if an interest rate cut looks more imminent," Simon Francis, an analyst with Nomura Indonesia, said last week.
Brokers said big-caps Gudang Garam, Telkom, Indocement and Sampoerna were among the targets of bargain-hunting.

"Improved sentiment prompted buying in Indocement, but there are unlikely to be many changes in the firm's fundamentals that could further boost the stock price," an analyst with a large local brokerage firm said.
The analyst said any possible cement price hikes this year were unlikely.
Indocement rose 75 rupiah to 3,300 rupiah with some 400,000 shares traded.
Big-capitalised toll road operator Citra Marga rose 75 rupiah to 2,125 rupiah in moderate trading.

Citra Lamtoro Gung, which has a stake in Citra Marga, signed an agrement on Monday with state-owned toll road operator Jasa Marga and state railway firm PT Perumka to build a 6.06 trillion rupiah urban transportation project in Jakarta.
Small-sized pharmaceutical distribution firm Soedarpo rose 100 rupiah to 2,100 rupiah with 56,000 shares changing hands in late trading.
State-owned financial firm PT Danareksa said on Monday it planned to acquire a 51-percent stake in Soedarpo, at a price of 2,275 rupiah per share.
The most active property firm Elang Realty rose 100 rupiah to 925 rupiah on local speculation, brokers said.
